body:
Spin-off from https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2063#issuecomment-2431653476

Current requirement:

| # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **4.1.3** | Verify that the principle of least privilege exists - users should only be able to access functions, data files, URLs, controllers, services, and other resources, for which they possess specific authorization. This implies protection against spoofing and elevation of privilege. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 285 |

For me the 4.1.3 is source for confusions for so many reasons. I think the reason is, that the first part of the requirement is abstract principle and other really-really-widespread test-case that covers basically everything.

So first move should be maybe to split it up and move the 2nd part away to V4.2.

Then we can come back to the question - what those principles like "least privileges" and "deny by default" gives us - how is it possible to test them etc, for that discussion I have opened other issue:

  * #2195

Also related discussion:

  * https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1934#issuecomment-2132122065

comments.body: I agree with Elar here. Well said.

2 things:
1. May you please assign this issue to me so that I can track it?
2. Is the split you are proposing to split out "This implies protection against spoofing and elevation of privilege"?
Oh,, I may have misunderstood - do you want to split out the examples of principle of least privilege?

Attempt to clarify the idea.

> Part 1: Verify that the principle of least privilege exists.

It's a principle and it requires further discussion, is it possible to test it.

> Part 2:  users should only be able to access functions, data files, URLs, controllers, services, and other resources, for which they possess specific authorization. 

It's an actionable requirement, mostly covers vertical vector, but it's not a clear separation from IDOR.

It requires further work:

  * should > must/can
  * users can access (availability) + user can only access (confidentiality, integrity)
  * _functions, data files, URLs, controllers, services, and other resources_ > services and resources
  * ~~specific~~

> Part 3: This implies protection against spoofing and elevation of privilege.

Not sure we need this part.

If we are modifying 4.2.1, please also consider this modified wording from Jim:

"_Verify that horizontal permission enforcement exists to ensure users are authorized to perform operations on specific items, preventing IDOR/BOLA attacks._" (See: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1934#issuecomment-2413765300)

What about:

"Verify that vertical access control exists such that users are only able to access functions, data files, URLs, controllers, services, and other resources for which they possess specific authorization."

And then use Jim's proposed language for an additional, separate requirement?
So thinking harder about this, it feels like this also needs to be part of the overall discussions on this chapter next week as there seems to be a few moving parts,
Yes, can we all meet after lunch and try to get v4 closer to completion please? We need at least 3 or more of us to drive this home.

We are going to split 4.1.3 into three parts (function, data and field level access control) and move the POLP principle to the description text. Here is my first attempt to make this happen.

**First, here is the new text for the top of the v4.**

The Principle of Least Privilege (POLP) in access control design ensures that users and systems are granted only the minimal level of access necessary to perform their tasks, reducing the risk of unauthorized actions or exposure of sensitive data. This implies protection against spoofing and elevation of privilege.

Second, here is the update to 4.1.3 dropping POLP and focusing on function level access control.

4.1.3 | Verify that the application ensures that function level access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions.  | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 285
-- | -- | -- | -- | -- | --

Third, here is the new to 4.2.1 (IDOR) and 4.1.8 (field level access control).

4.2.1 | Verify that the application ensures that data specific access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions to specific data items to mitigate insecure direct object reference (IDOR) and broken object level authorization (BOLA).  | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 285
-- | -- | -- | -- | -- | --

4.1.7 | Verify that the application ensures that field level access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions to specific fields to mitigate broken object property level authorization (BOPLA).  | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 285
-- | -- | -- | -- | -- | --

Thank you @ryarmst and @elarlang  for helping me wordsmith these.

Re-opening this for the draft stage because jim mentioned some chapter text that does not seem to have made it into the chapter:
https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2196#issuecomment-2459115103

Jim also said:
https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2584#issuecomment-2642885998

> 
> I see that we no longer mention "principle of least privilege" anywhere in https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blob/master/5.0/en/0x12-V4-Access-Control.md
> 
> May I suggest we add it to the introduction section? Perhaps change the intro from:
> 
> _Authorization is the process of allowing access only to permitted consumers (users, servers and other clients). Ensure that a verified application satisfies the following high-level requirements:_
> 
> : to : 
> 
> _Authorization ensures that access is granted only to permitted consumers (users, servers, and other clients). To enforce the Principle of Least Privilege (POLP), verified applications must meet the following requirements:_
> 
> ... or similar so it's at least mentioned?
>
My personal opinion is that we can mention this in surrounding text but not in a requirement as it is not really a testable principle.
Agreed. I am on it today. The PR is in.
